summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of Kathmandu, the capital and largest municipality of Nepal. It covers the city's administrative status, its place in the Kathmandu Valley urban agglomeration, and its geography and river. It also describes food and drink culture, ethnic and religious makeup, museums, and key historical and religious sites such as the Pashupatinath Temple and the National Museum.
one_line: Overview of Kathmandu, Nepal's capital and largest city, covering its geography, food, people, religions, museums and history.
key_facts: Kathmandu is the capital and largest municipality of Nepal and hosts the headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).
Kathmandu is the only city of Nepal with the administrative status of Mahanagar (Metropolitan City).
According to the 2011 census, Kathmandu Metropolitan City has a population of 975,453 and measures 49.45 km2 (19.09 sq mi).
Kathmandu is located to the north of the Bagmati River and has an average elevation of 1,400 metres (4,600 ft) above sea level.
Kathmandu had only one western-style restaurant in 1955.
American chop suey is a hybrid food developed to accommodate tourists in Kathmandu.
The Bagmati River is considered a holy river by both Hindus and Buddhists, and Hindus are cremated on its banks.
The National Museum was established in 1928 as a collection house of war trophies and weapons, originally named Chhauni Silkhana.
The largest ethnic groups in Kathmandu are Newar (29.6%), Matwali (25.1%), Khas Brahmins (20.51%) and Chettris (18.5%).
The major languages are Nepali and Nepal Bhasa, and the major religions are Hinduism and Buddhism.
Ailaa and thwon, alcohol made from rice, are the alcoholic beverages of Kathmandu, found in all the local bhattis.
The Gorkha Kingdom ended the Malla confederation after the Battle of Kathmandu in 1768, marking the beginning of the modern era in Kathmandu.
The Pashupatinath Temple is a 5th century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and is the oldest Hindu temple in Kathmandu.
The temple as it stands today was built in the 19th century, although the image of the bull and the black four-headed image of Pashupati are at least 300 years old.
Pashupatinath Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Shivaratri is its most important festival.
The National Museum is located near the Swayambhunath stupa in a building constructed in the early 19th century by General Bhimsen Thapa.
